approaches.name: Anterior approach to the capitellum
approaches.corridor: Between brachioradialis and brachialis after identification and mobilization of the radial nerve

sources.title: Comparison of lateral versus anterolateral approach for isolated capitellar shear fractures
Relation of the radial nerve to the anterior capsule of the elbow

procedure_applications.condition: A simple anterior capitellar fracture without posterior comminution requires direct anterior reduction and screw fixation

positioning.text: Position supine with arm on a hand table, elbow extendable, and forearm rotatable for nerve protection and imaging.

setup.text: Confirm by CT that posterior capitellar comminution is absent and prepare magnification and vessel-loop control of the radial nerve and branches.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark biceps lateral border, brachioradialis medial border, elbow crease, radial head, and lateral epicondyle.

incision.text: Use a curved anterior incision from the lateral biceps border proximally toward the medial brachioradialis border distally.

superficial_interval.text: Open biceps fascia, retract biceps medially, and identify and protect the lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve.

deep_interval.text: Develop brachioradialis-brachialis interval, identify radial nerve, trace it to PIN and superficial branch, then retract muscles with nerve protected before longitudinal capsulotomy.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous sensory plane, biceps fascia, brachialis-brachioradialis interval, radial-nerve plane, capsule, then capitellum.

structures_encountered.text: Lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve, biceps, brachialis, brachioradialis, radial nerve, PIN, superficial radial nerve, capsule, and capitellum are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Radial nerve and branches, lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve, brachial vessels medially, cartilage, and anterior capsule are at risk.

danger_zones.text: The radial nerve contacts capsule near the radial neck; avoid distal blind capsular dissection or prolonged anterior retraction.

retraction_hazards.text: Maintain direct nerve visualization and use broad intermittent retraction; do not lever over the radial head or neck.

exposure.text: Exposes anterior capitellum and lateral trochlear ridge with direct anterior-to-posterior fixation access.

limitations.text: Cannot visualize posterior capitellum and is unsuitable for posterior comminution or complex trochlear extension.

extensions.text: Convert to a lateral/extensile approach if posterior reduction cannot be assessed rather than extending blindly around the radial nerve.

indications.text: Use for simple anterior capitellar shear fractures without posterior comminution.

relative_contraindications.text: Avoid for posterior comminution, complex trochlear extension, or when radial-nerve mobilization is unsafe.

implant_implications.text: Allows perpendicular anterior fixation; countersink headless screws and confirm posterior exit and joint containment.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Use AP, lateral, oblique, and radiocapitellar views to confirm reduction, screw trajectory, and absence of posterior prominence.

closure.text: Repair capsule, release retractors and confirm radial-nerve continuity, then close fascia and skin in layers.

complications.text: Complications include radial/PIN palsy, sensory nerve injury, stiffness, fixation failure, avascular necrosis, heterotopic ossification, and arthritis.

bailouts.text: Convert to lateral exposure when posterior comminution is found or radial-nerve-safe visualization is inadequate.

questions.question: What fracture pattern is appropriate?
questions.answer: A simple capitellar fracture without posterior comminution.

questions.question: Which nerve must be traced to its branches?
questions.answer: The radial nerve to PIN and superficial radial nerve.

approaches.name: Lateral approach to the distal humerus
approaches.corridor: Subperiosteal lateral-column elevation with common-extensor split anterior to the lateral collateral ligament

sources.title: Are outcomes after fixation of distal humerus coronal shear fractures affected by surgical approach?
Capitellum fractures: should the collateral ligament be repaired primarily?

procedure_applications.condition: A lateral-condyle, epicondyle, capitellar, or lateral trochlear shear fracture needs direct lateral control

positioning.text: Position supine or lateral with elbow freely flexed and forearm rotatable for radial-nerve relaxation and imaging.

setup.text: Review CT for posterior comminution and trochlear extension; prepare for LCL repair or epicondyle osteotomy if exposure must be extended.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark lateral epicondyle, supracondylar ridge, radial head, olecranon, and common-extensor origin.

incision.text: Center incision on lateral epicondyle, extend proximally along supracondylar ridge and distally toward radial head in line with common extensors.

superficial_interval.text: Open deep fascia in line and elevate lateral-column muscle-capsule subperiosteally proximally.

deep_interval.text: Split common extensors anterior to the LCL and radial-head equator; preserve ligament unless planned release/osteotomy is required and repairable.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, deep fascia, common extensor origin, capsule, then lateral distal humerus.

structures_encountered.text: Common extensors, brachioradialis, LCL/LUCL, capsule, capitellum, trochlea, radial head, anconeus, and lateral triceps are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Radial nerve and PIN, LCL complex, articular cartilage, capitellar blood supply, and posterior interosseous structures are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Radial nerve divides near radial head; avoid prolonged or levered anterior retraction and do not split posterior to radial-head equator into LCL.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid anterior lever retractors and excessive traction near radial head/neck; protect cartilage and lateral blood supply.

exposure.text: Exposes lateral condyle, capitellum, lateral trochlea, and with posterior elevation the lateral column.

limitations.text: Medial trochlea and deep anterior surface may remain limited without LCL release, osteotomy, or another approach.

extensions.text: Elevate lateral triceps/anconeus posteriorly or perform repairable epicondyle osteotomy/LCL release to hinge the joint around intact MCL.

indications.text: Use for lateral condyle or epicondyle fractures and capitellar/trochlear coronal shear fractures.

relative_contraindications.text: Choose a broader posterior approach for complex bicondylar fractures and an anterior approach for selected isolated anterior fragments.

implant_implications.text: Supports headless articular screws and lateral-column fixation; any released LCL or osteotomized epicondyle requires stable repair.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Use AP, lateral, oblique, and radiocapitellar views to verify articular reduction, column fixation, and screw containment.

closure.text: Repair capsule and common extensors and anatomically repair LCL or epicondyle to prevent posterolateral rotatory instability.

complications.text: Complications include radial/PIN injury, PLRI, stiffness, heterotopic ossification, avascular necrosis, arthritis, nonunion, and fixation failure.

bailouts.text: Use planned osteotomy or alternate exposure when the trochlea/posterior surface remains unseen; never sacrifice LCL without secure repair.

questions.question: Where is the extensor split placed?
questions.answer: Anterior to the LCL and anterior to the radial-head equator.

questions.question: What retractor practice is avoided?
questions.answer: Levered or prolonged anterior retraction near radial head and neck.

questions.question: What must be repaired if released?
questions.answer: The LCL or lateral epicondyle to prevent PLRI.
